text: The youngest son of Uldan Dornworth left Coldton and settled in Elmmere.
Felde went along to live in Elmmere as well.
Riric Vellwood could keep it no longer and told Luena that the Vellmere mill ledger was rewritten after the flood.
Yera died of drowning in the flood at Wendby.
Zanelle Dornworth and Brerald were wed at Tormere, with half the parish looking on. The couple lived in Tormere from then on.
Late one night Ordrek confided to the wife of Zarald Hollaby that the old abbey at Torcombe hides a second cellar.
Late one night Riric Vellwood confided to Thibin Ashley that the Vellmere mill ledger was rewritten after the flood.
After the quarrel, Luena quit Coldton for good and took lodgings in Brynford.
Tarine Corraby left Dunholt and settled in Harrowstead.
Elwyn gave Yeten Dornworth a solemn promise to rebuild the fallen wall at Mirehaven.
act: to rebuild the fallen wall at Mirehaven

text: True to her word to Gaten Stenoway, Karine finished what she had promised (plant an orchard on the slope above Harrowstead).
Senelle Stenoway pressed the jade lantern into the hands of Dalis Vellmere and would take nothing for it.
A parcel from Aera Fellenridge reached Isdrek Vellmere; inside was the brass bell, now his to keep.
Illde Fellenridge packed a single trunk and moved from Dunholt to Elmwick.
Peten went along to live in Elmwick as well.
Ildette found work in Brynwick, moved there, and did not return to Salton.
Ildette Ashley broke faith with Aera Fellenridge, and the promised work (plant an orchard on the slope above Elmmere) was never begun.
Hawyn Vellmere and Dadan Fellworth were wed at Elmwick, with half the parish looking on. The couple lived in Elmwick from then on.
Vowyn Vellwood rode out of Coldton; by the next market day she was living in Elmmere.
Riric Vellwood went along to live in Elmmere as well.
Halis Fellenridge gave Orric a solemn promise to repair the roof of the chapel at Salton.
act: to repair the roof of the chapel at Salton

text: The husband of Karine Corraby left Elmwick and settled in Larkholt.
Karine went along to live in Larkholt as well.
Felde Hollaby gave the oak spyglass to Lame Elwyn.
Halis Fellenridge gave birth to a son, named Maric Dornworth; the father was Orric Dornworth. The family lived in Harrowstead.
Halis Fellenridge swore to Jovus Dornworth to carry a sealed letter to Larkholt, and shook on it.
act: to carry a sealed letter to Larkholt

text: The husband of Dalis Vellmere was apprenticed anew and became a cooper.
Old Senelle meant to go to Torcombe before the frost, but the roads flooded and the journey was put off.
In a letter that Yeten Dornworth burned after reading, Tavus Dornworth revealed that the old abbey at Torcombe hides a second cellar.
A rumor started by the wife of Riric Vellwood had it that Elvie Fellenridge was dead of plague; the wife of Riric Vellwood had it from a peddler.
Ildette Ashley died of a long wasting sickness at Brynwick.
Islis Corraby left Dunholt and settled in Elmmere.
Haric Corraby gave the ivory seal to Tavus Fellworth.
Gaten Stenoway could keep it no longer and told Kadette Stenoway that the bridge toll at Larkholt is skimmed every month.
Zanelle Dornworth rode out of Tormere; by the next market day she was living in Salton.
Brerald Dornworth went along to live in Salton as well.
In the chapel at Elmwick, Nyrald married Orwyn Dornworth. The couple lived in Elmwick from then on.
The eldest daughter of Nyssa Marrwood broke faith with Thibin Ashley, and the promised work (pay the old debt owed to the Ashley family) was never begun.
Late one night Ordrek Hollaby confided to Cossa Corraby that the deed to the Larkholt pastures was forged.
Ordrek Hollaby could keep it no longer and told Dadan that the deed to the Larkholt pastures was forged.
Late one night Isdrek Vellmere confided to Nyssa Marrwood that the fire at the Harrowstead granary was set on purpose.
The husband of Nyssa Marrwood swore to Luena Dornworth to rebuild the fallen wall at Coldton, and shook on it.
act: to rebuild the fallen wall at Coldton

text: A daughter was born to Elwyn Corraby and Yeten Dornworth, and they called the child Jora Dornworth. The family lived in Elmmere.
A rumor started by Islis had it that Yeten Dornworth was dead of plague; Islis had it from a peddler.
Tavus Dornworth talked for weeks of going to Wilcombe, yet in the end stayed where he was.
Yeten talked for weeks of going to Coldton, yet in the end stayed where he was.
A son was born to Rora Fellworth and Gadrek Marrwood, and they called the child Bretho Marrwood. The family lived in Mirehaven.
Brerald Dornworth swore to Zanelle Dornworth to plant an orchard on the slope above Brynwick, and shook on it.
act: to plant an orchard on the slope above Brynwick

text: Zanelle Dornworth gave up idleness and took work as a tanner.
Zanelle Dornworth found work in Wilcombe, moved there, and did not return to Salton.
Brerald went along to live in Wilcombe as well.
Felde Hollaby pressed the bone locket into the hands of Yeten and would take nothing for it.
They laid Senelle Stenoway in the churchyard at Harrowstead, dead of a wound that festered.
Peten rode out of Elmwick; by the next market day he was living in Salton.
Illde Fellenridge went along to live in Salton as well.
Hawyn was apprenticed anew and became a brewer.
Before the winter was out, Vorine Ashley took Brevus in marriage at Brynford. The couple lived in Brynford from then on.
Luena Dornworth gave the oak mirror to Vorine.
In a letter that Veslis burned after reading, Kadette revealed that the bridge toll at Larkholt is skimmed every month.
In a letter that the wife of Nyrald Hollaby burned after reading, Cossa revealed that the deed to the Larkholt pastures was forged.
The wife of Brevus Dornworth pressed the oak mirror into the hands of the husband of Nyssa Marrwood and would take nothing for it.
Islis Corraby swore to Tavus Dornworth to pay the old debt owed to the Vellwood family, and shook on it.
act: to pay the old debt owed to the Vellwood family

text: Elwyn Corraby packed a single trunk and moved from Elmmere to Wilcombe.
Yeten followed her to Wilcombe within the month.
In a letter that Luena Dornworth burned after reading, Nyssa Marrwood revealed that the fire at the Harrowstead granary was set on purpose.
They laid Luvie Fellenridge in the churchyard at Dunholt, dead of old age, quietly in sleep.
Elvie Fellenridge, whatever the gossips said, was seen hale and well at the summer fair in Dunholt.
